title: Against the market baseline, the skill score is negative everywhere
headline_insight: The model's Brier Skill Score versus the market is negative across every sport -- MLB overall -0.1043, soccer -0.7039 -- so the model does not beat the market, and that null is the exhibit's whole point.
what_it_means: Brier Skill Score is 1 minus Brier over a reference Brier; positive means you beat the reference. Against climatology (a constant base-rate guess) the MLB model scores clearly positive (+0.3327), as any real in-game model should; on the far smaller soccer corpus it is negative (-0.8569), meaning the model there does not even beat the base rate. Against the market it is negative in every sport and every checkpoint -- the market's Brier is lower. This is reported plainly, not hidden.
how_to_read: Read each cell's BSS: above 0 beats the baseline, below 0 loses to it; compare the vs-market column (the hard test) against the vs-climatology column (the easy one).
why_it_matters: It is the cleanest single statement of the project thesis -- the market is efficient; the MLB model crushes the base rate but does not out-predict the market.
caveat: The most negative MLB cell is mid(inn4-6) at -0.1133, and late(inn7+) is now the least negative at -0.0918; these are revision-2 figures measured on the segment-clean corpus (27,351 MLB rows, 4,265 soccer rows).

cited.value: BSS vs market is near or below 0 across sports and checkpoints -- the model does not beat the closing reference forecast's Brier. That null result is the POINT of this exhibit, not a defect. BSS vs climatology is strongly positive (model and market both crush the base-rate baseline), which is expected for in-game win-prob and is NOT an advantage. Truth source: docs/JOB_EVIDENCE_PACKET.md.
